05
Arrival

Getting into Hong Kong

Smooth sailing through immigration — here's what you need to know before you land.

Victoria Harbour
1

Visa-free for most

Nationals of most countries do not require a visa to enter Hong Kong for tourism and can stay for periods varying from seven to 180 days, depending on nationality. If you're unsure of your status, please check with any Chinese embassy or consulate.

Embassy ↗Consulate ↗
2

No arrival cards

All visitors are not required to complete or submit the arrival or departure card for immigration in Hong Kong.

3

Fast-track with e-Channel

For frequent visitors to Hong Kong, you may be eligible to fast track the immigration lines.

eChannel Services ↗

Getting There

Three easy ways to the hotel

The SkyCity precinct

Terminal 2, AsiaWorld-Expo, SkyPier, 11 SKIES and the SkyCity Marriott — all within walking distance.

Hotel ↔ Airport Every 30 mins

Terminal 2, Coach Station Bays 9–15

Hotel departures05:00 – 00:30
Airport departures05:15 – 00:45
Hotel ↔ Tung Chung MRT Exit A Every 30 mins
Hotel departures08:00 – 22:30
Tung Chung departures08:15 – 22:45
  • Take the Airport Express to AsiaWorld-Expo Station, then a 2-minute walk via the covered footbridge.
  • Sky Pier and Terminals 1 and 2 are within the same SkyCity precinct.
  • Bus S1 drops at the hotel / SkyCity Interchange.
    S1
  • These routes drop at the SKYCITY Transport Terminal — about a 7-minute walk.
    A23A33XB4E11E11AE21E21DE22E22AE22PE22XE32E36PE41S56
  • Driving: Tsing Ma Bridge, Route 8 or Tuen Mun–Chek Lap Kok Tunnel toward Airport / AsiaWorld-Expo.
